Twelve centuries of Egypt, twelve at a time

A handlist of the Cleveland Museum of Art's Egyptian objects from the New Kingdom to the Late Period, 1550 to 332 BCE, oldest first. Its pages are counted on a senet board: faience squares from a tomb at Abydos, made in the reign of Thutmose III, with one of the board's own pieces standing on the page you are reading.

The game, in six notes

Passing

Senet means “passing”. It was played in Egypt for some three thousand years, from before the first dynasties to the Roman period: thirty squares in three rows of ten, two players, a handful of pieces each.

# senet Pagination on a senet board. The control is a real `
    ` of page links (Previous, numbered pages with the current one marked `aria-current="page"`, Next). Above it lies a photograph of an Egyptian senet board, faience tiles from a tomb at Abydos made in the reign of Thutmose III (the Met, 01.4.1a), and one of **that board's own pieces**, photographed from straight above in the same campaign, stands on the square that is the current page. Go to another page and the piece is moved there the way a player moves it: a move of one to five squares (what a throw of the sticks can give) is counted out square by square along the board's S, each hop rising under gravity and coming down with a knock; a longer move is lifted, carried across the board in the air and set down. Nothing is drawn. The board is the ``; the piece is an ``; its shadow is the piece's own silhouette. At rest, what you see is the photograph with a real piece on it. ```html
    1. ‹ Previous
    2. 1
    3. 2
    4. 3
    5. …
    6. 41
    7. Next ›
      …Previous,
    1. 1 / 6
      2. , Next…
    ``` ```js import { senet, squareOf, windowed } from './senet.js'; const s = nav.senet; // auto-started controller (or senet(nav, opts) yourself; the same one comes back) s.go(12); // move to page 12 (pushes ?page=12 unless history is 'none') s.page; s.pages; // live s.setPages(50); // the list grew s.hold(); s.advance(120); // stills: freeze, then step the simulation by hand (ms) s.release(); s(); // destroy: removes listeners, the shadow, the tip and the live region nav.addEventListener('senet:change', (e) => e.detail); // {page, from, pages, square}: render that page here nav.addEventListener('senet:knock', (e) => e.detail); // {square, force 0..1}: the piece touched down nav.addEventListener('senet:settle', (e) => e.detail); // {page}: it is at rest ``` ## Options | attribute | option | default | | |---|---|---|---| | `data-pages` | `pages` | 1 | how many pages | | `data-page` | `page` | the URL's `?`, else `data-page`, else the `aria-current` link, else 1 | the current page | | `data-href` | `href` | `?page={n}` | each link's href; `{n}` is the page | | `data-param` | `param` | `page` | the query parameter read on load and on Back/Forward | | `data-history` | `history` | `push` | `push` / `replace`: the component handles the click, updates the URL and fires `senet:change` (you render the page). `none`: no URL change. `load`: the links navigate normally (a multi-page site); the page you left is kept in `sessionStorage`, and the new page's piece starts on its old square and walks to the new one | | `data-around` | `around` | 2, or 1 when the nav is under 520 px | pages either side of the current one in the list | | `data-label` | `label` | `Page` | the word in the live announcement ("Page 4 of 41") | | class `sn-compact` | `compact` | | Previous, the small board, Next; "4 / 41" under the board | | class `sn-spool` on `.sn-piece` | | | use the spool (`assets/spool.webp`) instead of the cone | ## Squares and pages Thirty squares, played in the S the Egyptians played them in: 1–10 along the top row left to right, 11–20 back along the middle, 21–30 along the bottom. Their centres were measured on the photograph (`tools/cut.py` → `assets/board.json`, copied into `SQUARES` in `senet.js`). Without JS, write the current square's centre into the piece's `--x` / `--y` (fractions of the board image). - **30 pages or fewer**: page *n* is square *n*; the squares after the last page stay empty. - **More than 30**: the last five pages always take the marked squares 26–30 (the house of beauty, the water, and the squares off the board), and the pages before them share squares 1–25 evenly (`squareOf`). On a long list the piece's place is how far through you are, and the end of the series is the end of the game. A page change that stays on the same square still answers: the piece is lifted (0.26 s in the air, about three quarters of its width) and set down where it was, with the same `senet:knock`. Why not a windowed mapping (the current page and its neighbours always on squares of their own): with more than 30 pages no fixed mapping can give every page its own square, so a windowed one would have to depend on the path you took, and the same URL would show the piece in different places. The even share keeps one page, one place. The list under the board is the control and the tap target (44 px tall, at least 34 px wide). With a pointer, the squares are targets too: hovering one shows the page or pages it holds, and clicking goes there. ## In life, and here | In life | Here | |---|---| | A senet board is thirty squares in three rows of ten, played as an S: along the top, back along the middle, along the bottom. This one is faience tiles from tomb D99 at Abydos (reign of Thutmose III, ca. 1479–1425 BCE), set by the museum into a modern wooden box 43 cm long. | The Met's straight-down photograph of it (01.4.1a_EGDP013652, 4000 px), cropped to the box top and cut along its four straight edges. Scaled, never redrawn. The squares' centres are measured on it; the piece only ever moves between them along the S. | | The last squares are marked. Here 26 has three *nefer* signs (the house of beauty), 27 water, 28 part of a sign. | The last five pages of a long list always land on 26–30. | | The pieces are cones and spools of blue faience marbled in black, about half a tile across, kept in the box's drawer. | One cone (or one spool in the compact variant), from the same set, photographed straight down in the same campaign and matted. Its size is half a tile, the ratio measured on the Met's three-quarter view DP310299, where these pieces stand on this board. On a small board (a phone) it is never drawn under 23 px (`--sn-min`), nor over 82% of a tile, so it stays a piece and never covers the dividers; its shadow keeps at least 1.2 px of offset and blur there, to stand it off the pale tiles. | | A move is cast with four throw sticks: one to five squares. The player counts the squares out, touching each. | A move of one to five squares is counted out: each square is a hop, up under gravity (90 piece-diameters/s², 0.2 s in the air, rising about half its width) while a critically damped spring on the hand carries it across, then a knock (`senet:knock`) and a 50 ms pause before the next. | | A piece moved further than a throw (setting up, putting away) is picked up and carried. | More than five squares: a spring lifts it to about one piece-width above the board, a slower critically damped spring carries it straight to the square in the air, and a third lowers it until the board stops it. | | Lifted, the piece comes nearer the eye and its shadow leaves it. | As it rises it grows by up to 12% (the camera is straight above) and its shadow, the same image blackened and blurred, falls further off and softer. | | | Fixed steps at 240 Hz inside `requestAnimationFrame`; the loop runs only while the piece moves. | ## Accessibility - A `
    ` with your `aria-label`, an `
      ` of real links, `aria-current="page"`, `rel="prev"` / `rel="next"`, Previous / Next as `` on the first and last page. - The board is `aria-hidden`: it is the picture of the control, the list is the control. - A polite live region says "Page 4 of 41" after each change. Focus stays where it was: on Previous / Next if you pressed one, else on the new current page. - Back and Forward move the piece (popstate). - Reduced motion: the piece is on its square at once. - Without JS: the links work as links, and the piece stands where `--x` / `--y` put it. ## Theming `--ink`, `--ink-2`, `--ink-3`, `--rule`, `--paper`, `--serif`, `--sans` as everywhere; `--sn-max` is the board's widest (1040 px, 300 px compact). The current page is underlined in the faience's own turquoise (`#1aa5a6`). ## Files - `assets/board.webp` (2400 × 755, 0.55 MB), `assets/board-1200.webp` (0.12 MB), `assets/cone.webp`, `assets/spool.webp`, `assets/board.json` (squares, piece sizes), `assets/credits.json`, `assets/PICK.md`. - `assets/catalogue/`, `assets/catalogue.json`: the demo's handlist only (483 Cleveland Museum of Art objects, CC0). - `tools/cut.py`: board crop and alpha, square measurement, piece mattes and scale. `tools/catalogue.py`: the demo's handlist. `tools/demo_page1.py`: writes page 1 of the handlist into `demo.html`, so it is a page without JS. ## Sound None yet. `senet:knock` fires on every touchdown with a force, for a recorded knock of faience on faience to be wired to with the studio's sound tool. No real recording of a small ceramic piece on a tile turned up (Commons has door knocks), and a synthesized click would be worse than silence. ## Credits Board and pieces: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Gameboard and Gaming Pieces, 01.4.1a–p, Gift of Egypt Exploration Fund, 1901, CC0. Handlist: The Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access, CC0. Matte: BiRefNet via the asset engine (`tools/engine/stages/matte.py`). Details in `assets/credits.json`.

# senet: the pick

Contact sheets (scratch, `tools/engine/jobs/`):
- `round9-lead-hunt/sheet-senet.jpg`: the lead's first pass, 24 previews (Met 553268, 548482, throw sticks 544500, 559444).
- `senet-hunt/sheet-met-orig.jpg`: 23 Met originals, full size: the three senet boxes the Met photographed (553268 ivory
  and ebony, 548482 Taia's, 544775 faience), Neferkhawet's cones and spools (35.3.x), Nefertari playing (DT11770).
- `senet-hunt/sheet-faience-pieces.jpg`: 11 views of the faience board's own cones and spools (01.4.1b–p), from the
  same campaign as the board, several straight down.
- `senet-hunt/sheet-others.jpg`: 27 Commons candidates: Turin's double board S 8451 (CC0, 7360 px), Walters 48408 and
  its pieces, Brooklyn's Amenhotep III board 49.56, Tutankhamun's boxes (Cairo, Paris), Louvre E 913, Berlin, Nubian
  Museum, Deir el-Medina (NMEC), Brooklyn's lion-headed pieces, a Walters lintel with game players.
- `senet-work/sheet-crops.jpg`: 16 crops of single pieces seen from above, and `senet-work/sheet-cut.jpg`, four mattes.

About 85 views of some 25 objects. Met search ("senet", "game box", "gaming piece", "throw stick", "knucklebone")
listed 97 object ids; the Met's object API began refusing requests partway (other builders were hunting at the same
time), so the later records were reached through Commons file names and the Met's image server. `engine.py inspect`
ran on every Met original: all PASS except a "near-perfect symmetry" warning on two square-on views (a game box seen
square-on is symmetric) and the Nefertari facsimile (1885 px, used only in prose).

## The board: Met 01.4.1a, faience, Abydos, reign of Thutmose III

**Gameboard and Gaming Pieces**, ca. 1479–1425 BCE, from tomb D99 in cemetery D at Abydos (Egypt Exploration Fund),
Gift of the EEF, 1901, CC0. Thirty tiles of turquoise and pale blue faience, set by the museum into a modern wooden
box (43 × 13.5 cm). The bottom row is the end of the game, and it is marked: square 26 with three *nefer* signs, 27
with water, 28 with a fragment of a sign. Several tiles are mended from fragments, and five carry a round blue
patch. All of it is shown as it is.

- `01.4.1a_EGDP013652.jpg`: the senet face straight down, 4000 × 2250, the box top 3245 px across (75 px/cm), tiles
  250 px. Its edges are straight to within 0.2° of the frame, so it is cropped, not rotated.
- Its own pieces, from the same campaign (EGDP013654–13665), lying on the same grey, several of them **straight
  down**: cones as a spiral of black in blue around the tip, spools as flat marbled discs.
- DP310299 (a later campaign, three-quarter) shows those pieces standing on that board. That fixes the scale: a
  piece is about half a tile across (about 1.65 cm).

### Why this one, not the others

| object | what it has | why not |
|---|---|---|
| **Met 01.4.1a–p, faience, Abydos** | the senet face straight down at 4000 px, sharp; its own cones and spools photographed straight down in the same campaign; the end squares marked | **picked** |
| Met 553268 (16.10.475), ebony and ivory, with its pieces 16.10.475b–k | a beautiful box; its 3×10 face (`16.10.475a.bot`) is seen from slightly in front, 3400 px | the pieces were only photographed lying beside the box, at an angle (DP160290); none from above |
| Met 548482, Taia's box | its faience pieces photographed from above, standing on the board (EGDP012977) | that face is the game of twenty squares, not senet; 2000 px; the senet face is only seen at an angle |
| Turin S 8451, double board (Commons, CC0, 7360 px) | very large, sharp, wooden pieces and a drawer | the senet face is never straight down; pieces only at three-quarter |
| Brooklyn 49.56, Amenhotep III | glorious blue faience, pieces beside it | three-quarter only, 1536 px |
| Walters 48408 | a straight-down senet face | worn grey faience, 1800 px, its pieces from another set |
| Tutankhamun's boxes, Louvre E 913, Berlin, Nubian Museum, NMEC | famous | visitors' photographs through glass, at angles, CC BY-SA |
| Met 35.3.x, Neferkhawet's cones and spools | 3200 × 4000, sharp | side views only, and not this board's set |

### Throw sticks

Met 544500 and 559437–559444 are lovely (ivory, tinted red on one face). The brief says to use them only if
they earn their place. They don't here: the pager moves where the reader asks, so a throw would be decoration. What
the sticks give is the rule of the motion: a throw is one to five, so a move of one to five squares is counted out
square by square, and anything longer is lifted and carried.
